messages:
maria.gonzalez: spotting a weird perf + numerics regression in canary. after the kernel-selector change, paged-attn using the fp8-flash variant started returning inf/NaN for certain long-prefix chat traces. repro is fairly consistent with long prefixes (>=1024) + repeated KV reuse across microbatches.

aj: can you paste the profiler traces and a minimal snippet?

maria.gonzalez: pasted the important bits below. profiler shows a big spike in exp(max) counts right before the crash, and the kernel runtime jumps ~2.3x for that batch.

```
# profiler extract
2026-03-15T18:42:01Z  paged_attn::flash_fp8  kernel_ms=4.8  exp_max=1.2e3  inf_count=0
2026-03-15T18:42:01Z  paged_attn::flash_fp8  kernel_ms=12.6 exp_max=2.1e4  inf_count=17  -> OOM/NaN downstream
2026-03-15T18:42:01Z  paged_attn::bf16_fused   kernel_ms=9.1  exp_max=800     inf_count=0
```

maria.gonzalez: repro snippet (pseudo):
```
# reuse KV across requests, microbatching
for req in stream:
  kv_cache.append(chunk)
  out = flash_fp8_attn(q, kv_cache, ...)
```

aj: interesting. sounds like fp8 dynamic range zippering when the sequence length distribution changes mid-batch and the kernel's per-block scaling isn't being recomputed. did kernel-selector recently enable a "reuse-scale" fast-path?

maria.gonzalez: yes — kernel-selector picks flash_fp8 for most short-window workloads and we have a heuristic that keeps fp8 scaling state if next batch seq_len within hysteresis. intended to avoid recomputing scales on stable workloads. but with paged-attn the effective logits distribution changes as the prefix grows -> overflow.

suresh: two directions: (1) short-term mitigation: disable fp8 fast-path/hysteresis for paged-attn & long-prefix (>512) traces; (2) longer-term: add a numeric guard (clamp/log-sum-exp stable trick) inside the flash_fp8 wrapper and recompute per-block max when KV changed.

jonathan: agree. also add a kernel-selection feature flag so we can rollback per-customer quickly. please add a perf regression test asserting no inf/NaN and check kernel_ms variance.

lee: quick note — bf16 fallback is slightly slower but stable; we should update batching heuristic too. current batching groups by avg_seq_len which misses high prefix skew. if we bias grouping to max_seq_len for paged-KV workloads, fewer cross-batch numeric surprises.

maria.gonzalez: here's a proposed minimal guard to land ASAP (pseudo):
```
// before softmax in fp8 path
float m = max(logits);
for i: logits[i] -= m;          // standard stability shift
clamp_logits = clamp(logits, -kCLAMP, +kCLAMP); // kCLAMP tuned for fp8 dynamic range
softmax = exp(clamp_logits) / sum(exp(clamp_logits));
```

aj: two comments: (A) the clamp constant must be per-block and tuned to quantization scale, don't hard-code, compute from current fp8 scale params; (B) also track per-block peak and emit a metric so rollout can detect when fp8 is repeatedly clamped (signal to fallback or re-quantize).

maria.gonzalez: will put together a tiny change: disable hysteresis for fp8 with paged-attn + add clamp + metric emit. patch and perf unit tests by EOD. will also open a short-lived feature-flagged canary.

infra-bot: canary created: canary/attn-fp8-guard/2026-03-15, will apply to 10% hosts across us-west-2.

aj: for the longer fix, perf team should run an A/B with bf16_fused vs fp8_flash with the clamp and new per-block-recompute policy. need throughput and p99 latency per model. also add a synthetic test that grows prefix over time to surface regressions.

suresh: i'll own the perf runs. maria, ping me when patch lands. i'll add the synthetic prefix growth trace to the eval harness.

maria.gonzalez: patch pushed to PR #4521 (fp8: disable-hysteresis-paged-attn + clamp + metric). unit tests added: test_no_nan_long_prefix, test_recompute_on_kv_change.

lee: thanks. after canary, if metrics look good, let's update kernel-selector thresholds: avoid fp8 for max_seq_len > 768 unless model-specific verified. also update docs/notes in kernel selector file.

maria.gonzalez: noted. will follow up with rollout plan and perf numbers once canary finishes (~2h).

aj: great. summary: immediate guard + disable hysteresis for paged-attn, canary, perf runs, and then a measured rollback/fix if clamp causes accuracy regressions. :thumbsup:

suresh: adding an integration test to run nightly to avoid regression next time.

maria.gonzalez: thanks everyone, will report results in this thread.
